messages:
Maya (Finance): Invoice from CloudTools UG — vendor applied 20% Estonian VAT (EE987654321) on dedicated capacity invoice #CT-2025-04. Attached PDF.
Luca (AP): We can't reclaim EE VAT in DE. If this is a B2B supply to a non-EU business, vendor should not use OSS. Need clarification of vendor registration and place of supply.
Hans (Vendor Ops): CloudTools says legal seat Germany but they're registered for OSS in Estonia and used that number. They charged 20% on the invoice. We're billed to Redwood Inc (US) with US billing address.
Maya (Finance): We're a US entity (EIN 12-3456789). My understanding: for digital/hosting services supplied to a non-EU business, vendor should not charge EU VAT. TaxBot, confirm?
TaxBot: Rule: For supplies of telecom/digital services, OSS is for B2C EU consumption. For B2B supplies to non-EU business, place of supply is customer - outside EU - VAT not due. Vendor applied OSS incorrectly. See: https://ec.europa.eu/taxation_customs/vies/ and OSS guidance.
Annie (Legal): Confirmed. Ask vendor to reissue a credit note + corrected invoice without VAT. Wording to include: 'Supply to non-EU business — VAT not applicable' and our US tax ID. Also ask them to keep a record for OSS corrections.
Luca (AP): I'll draft the vendor email and request reissue. No gross-up or WHT here — this is VAT correction only.
Hans (Vendor Ops): Draft to vendor: "Hi CloudTools — Invoice CT-2025-04 shows Estonian VAT charged. Redwood Inc is a US business (EIN: 12-3456789) and should not be charged EU VAT for B2B supply. Please issue a credit note and a corrected invoice without VAT, including statement 'Supply to non-EU business — VAT not applicable'. Attach both docs for our records. Thanks."
Maya (Finance): LGTM, sending now. :white_check_mark:
Annie (Legal): Add request to keep original invoice date mapping on corrected docs to avoid ledger mismatch. :thumbsup:
